sections.title: What is a Basis?
lecture_lines: A basis is a set of vectors spanning a space.
These vectors must be linearly independent.
Any vector has a unique representation using basis vectors.
The standard basis in 2D is e1 = [1,0] and e2 = [0,1].
Coordinates are the coefficients in the unique linear combination.

sections.title: Why Change Basis?
lecture_lines: A change of basis re-expresses vectors in a new coordinate system.
We use a change-of-basis matrix for this conversion.
This matrix transforms coordinates from one basis to another.
It's formed by the new basis vectors expressed in the old basis.
This allows us to work with simpler or more convenient bases.
animations: Appear: Changing basis simplifies vector representation.
Highlight: New basis may align better with problem.
Scale up: This can make calculations easier.
Fade in: Show a vector in the original basis.
Fade in: Show the same vector in a new basis.

sections.title: The Transition Matrix: The Bridge
lecture_lines: The change-of-basis matrix converts coordinates between bases.
It's constructed using the new basis vectors as columns.
These vectors are expressed in terms of the original basis.
Multiplying a vector's old coordinates by this matrix yields new coordinates.
This matrix is crucial for transformations involving different bases.
